title: Tree-String Problem
statementMd:
A *rooted tree* is a non-directed connected graph without any cycles with a distinguished vertex, which is called the tree root. Consider the vertices of a rooted tree, that consists of $*n*$ vertices, numbered from 1 to $*n*$. In this problem the tree root is the vertex number 1.

Let's represent the length of the shortest by the number of edges path in the tree between vertices $*v*$ and $*u*$ as $*d*(*v*, *u*)$.

A *parent* of vertex $*v*$ in the rooted tree with the root in vertex $*r*$ $(*v* ≠ *r*)$ is vertex $*p*_{*v*}$, such that $*d*(*r*, *p*_{*v*}) + 1 = *d*(*r*, *v*)$ and **$*d*(*p*_{*v*}, *v*) = 1$**. For example, on the picture the parent of vertex $*v* = 5$ is vertex $*p*_{5} = 2$.

One day Polycarpus came across a rooted tree, consisting of $*n*$ vertices. The tree wasn't exactly ordinary: it had strings written on its edges. Polycarpus positioned the tree on the plane so as to make all edges lead from top to bottom if you go from the vertex parent to the vertex (see the picture). For any edge that lead from vertex $*p*_{*v*}$ to vertex $*v*$ $(1 < *v* ≤ *n*)$, he knows string $*s*_{*v*}$ that is written on it. All strings are written on the edges from top to bottom. For example, on the picture $*s*_{7}$="`ba`". The characters in the strings are numbered starting from 0.

![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/2358a87b1302583cb41f1d8aa514a32b02f411ec.png) An example of Polycarpus's tree (corresponds to the example from the statement)

Polycarpus defines the *position* in this tree as a specific letter on a specific string. The position is written as a pair of integers $(*v*, *x*)$ that means that the position is the $*x*$-th letter of the string $*s*_{*v*}$ ($1 < *v* ≤ *n*$, $0 ≤ *x* < |*s*_{*v*}|$), where $|*s*_{*v*}|$ is the length of string $*s*_{*v*}$. For example, the highlighted letters are positions ($2, 1$) and ($3, 1$).

Let's consider the pair of positions $(*v*, *x*)$ and $(*u*, *y*)$ in Polycarpus' tree, such that the way from the first position to the second goes down on each step. We will consider that the pair of such positions defines string $*z*$. String $*z*$ consists of all letters on the way from $(*v*, *x*)$ to $(*u*, *y*)$, written in the order of this path. For example, in the picture the highlighted positions define string "`bacaba`".

Polycarpus has a string $*t*$, he wants to know the number of pairs of positions that define string $*t*$. Note that the way from the first position to the second in the pair must go down everywhere. Help him with this challenging tree-string problem!

## Input

The first line contains integer $*n*$ $(2 ≤ *n* ≤ 10^{5})$ — the number of vertices of Polycarpus's tree. Next $*n* - 1$ lines contain the tree edges. The $*i*$-th of them contains number $*p*_{*i* + 1}$ and string $*s*_{*i* + 1}$ $(1 ≤ *p*_{*i* + 1} ≤ *n*; *p*_{*i* + 1} ≠ (*i* + 1))$. String $*s*_{*i* + 1}$ is non-empty and consists of lowercase English letters. The last line contains string $*t*$. String $*t*$ consists of lowercase English letters, its length is at least 2.

It is guaranteed that the input contains at most $3·10^{5}$ English letters.

## Output

Print a single integer — the required number.

Please, do not use the `%lld` specifier to read or write 64-bit integers in С++. It is preferred to use the `cin`, `cout` streams or the `%I64d` specifier.

## Note

In the first test case string "`aba`" is determined by the pairs of positions: (2, 0) and (5, 0); (5, 2) and (6, 1); (5, 2) and (3, 1); (4, 0) and (4, 2); (4, 4) and (4, 6); (3, 3) and (3, 5).

Note that the string is not defined by the pair of positions (7, 1) and (5, 0), as the way between them doesn't always go down.
statementZhMd:
<statement>

*有根树*是一个无向连通且无环的图，其中有一个被指定的顶点，称为树根。考虑一棵由 $*n*$ 个顶点组成的有根树，顶点编号为 1 到 $*n*$。在本题中，树根为编号 1 的顶点。

我们将树中顶点 $*v*$ 和 $*u*$ 之间最短路径的边数记为 $*d*(*v*, *u*)$。

在以顶点 $*r*$ 为根的有根树中，顶点 $*v*$ 的*父亲*（$*v* ≠ *r*$）是顶点 $*p*_{*v*}$，满足 $*d*(*r*, *p*_{*v*}) + 1 = *d*(*r*, *v*)$ 且 **$*d*(*p*_{*v*}, *v*) = 1$**。例如，在图中，顶点 $*v* = 5$ 的父亲是顶点 $*p*_{5} = 2$。

一天，Polycarpus 遇到了一棵由 $*n*$ 个顶点组成的有根树。这棵树并不普通：它的边上写有字符串。Polycarpus 将树放置在平面上，使得从顶点的父亲走向该顶点时，所有边都从上向下延伸（如图所示）。对于从顶点 $*p*_{*v*}$ 到顶点 $*v*$ 的每条边（$1 < *v* ≤ *n*$），他知道边上写着的字符串 $*s*_{*v*}$。所有字符串都沿着从上到下的方向书写。例如，在图中 $*s*_{7}$="`ba`"。字符串中的字符从 0 开始编号。

![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/2358a87b1302583cb41f1d8aa514a32b02f411ec.png) Polycarpus 的树的一个示例（对应题面中的示例）

Polycarpus 将树中的*位置*定义为某个字符串中的某个特定字母。位置表示为一对整数 $(*v*, *x*)$，表示字符串 $*s*_{*v*}$ 中下标为 $*x*$ 的字母（$1 < *v* ≤ *n*$，$0 ≤ *x* < |*s*_{*v*}|$），其中 $|*s*_{*v*}|$ 是字符串 $*s*_{*v*}$ 的长度。例如，图中高亮的字母对应位置 ($2, 1$) 和 ($3, 1$)。

考虑 Polycarpus 的树中的两个位置 $(*v*, *x*)$ 和 $(*u*, *y*)$，并且从第一个位置到第二个位置的路径每一步都向下。我们认为这两个位置定义了字符串 $*z*$。字符串 $*z*$ 由从 $(*v*, *x*)$ 到 $(*u*, *y*)$ 的路径上的所有字母组成，顺序按照路径上的先后排列。例如，图中高亮的位置定义了字符串 "`bacaba`"。

Polycarpus 有一个字符串 $*t*$，他想知道定义出字符串 $*t*$ 的位置对数量。注意，位置对中的路径必须始终向下。请帮助他解决这个具有挑战性的树字符串问题！

## 输入格式

第一行包含一个整数 $*n*$（$2 ≤ *n* ≤ 10^{5}$）——Polycarpus 的树的顶点数。接下来的 $*n* - 1$ 行包含树的边。第 $*i*$ 行包含整数 $*p*_{*i* + 1}$ 和字符串 $*s*_{*i* + 1}$（$1 ≤ *p*_{*i* + 1} ≤ *n*; *p*_{*i* + 1} ≠ (*i* + 1)）。字符串 $*s*_{*i* + 1}$ 非空，仅由小写英文字母组成。最后一行包含字符串 $*t*$。字符串 $*t*$ 由小写英文字母组成，且长度至少为 2。

保证输入中包含的英文字母总数不超过 $3·10^{5}$。

## 输出格式

输出一个整数——所求的数量。

请不要在 C++ 中使用 `%lld` 格式说明符读写 64 位整数。建议使用 `cin`、`cout` 流或 `%I64d` 格式说明符。

## 说明

在第一个测试用例中，字符串 "`aba`" 由以下位置对确定：(2, 0) 和 (5, 0)；(5, 2) 和 (6, 1)；(5, 2) 和 (3, 1)；(4, 0) 和 (4, 2)；(4, 4) 和 (4, 6)；(3, 3) 和 (3, 5)。

注意，位置对 (7, 1) 和 (5, 0) 并不能定义该字符串，因为它们之间的路径并非始终向下。
</statement>
